title: Behavior: the Hunter agent and fighting
tagline: The agent herself: every look, every throw, every kill counted and placed
summary: The Hunter is the in-game character as an agent: it owns her senses (every look), her keys, her looter and the books kept after every look and throw. On it sit the fight loops (clear a spot, kill one monster, shoot what's in the way while travelling), each throw's attack choice, the kill ledger and drop store, and the grind's target-first planner. Higher layers pick objectives; this slice makes the second-by-second decisions and keeps the counts they read.
details_md:
This slice is the agent itself. A higher layer (the hunt loop, a tour, a grind) picks an objective; the code here makes
the second-by-second decisions and keeps the books those layers read.

### Words used here
- **Look**: one `Scene` from `Senses.look`: where she is on the map, the monsters (each with a feed **track** id),
  her HP/MP bars, drops, and the events the perception service saw frame by frame since the last look.
- **The feed**: the perception service's stream of frame states (15 a second); its **tracker** follows each monster
  frame to frame and binds each EXP gain to the monster her attack took.
- **Lucky Seven**: the thief's skill, two stars a cast for MP; the **regular attack** is one star, no MP. Up close
  either key swipes with her claw instead.
- **Attack lock**: after an attack key the game ignores the next attack or jump for 730 ms (`COMBAT.attack_lock_ms`).
- **Mark**: a monster she has thrown at, followed look by look by `Attacks`.

### The Hunter is a hub of observers
`Hunter.__init__` builds everything once per hunting command (`gamelab/__main__.py`'s `_hunter`, or the simulator's
`Sim.hunter`): her `Senses` (every look), her `Actions` (her keys), a `Looter`, a `Report`, her pet's care, the ledger
trio (`Ledger`, `DropStore`, `Wounds`), her `Memory` of monsters, the map's `SpawnClock`, her `Aggro` belief, her
`Attacks` (each throw's key), the out-of-darts watch and the key-doubt watches. It then hangs 14 listeners on
`Senses.listeners` and 7 on `Actions.throw_listeners`. Every look goes through `Hunter.look`, and every throw through
`Actions`, so the books stay right **whoever** looks or throws: a fight, the navigator, the looter or the hunt loop.

### A kill is her EXP going up
The one rule everything rests on: a monster vanishing is not a kill (hit monsters flinch and hide under their damage
numbers, other players kill monsters too; about half the "kills" counted by vanishing weren't hers). A kill is her EXP
number rising, and the gain's size names which kind it can be (`localization.gains`). The `Ledger` places each gain on
a monster of that kind: the one the perception service's tracker bound it to, else one in the path of a throw keyed
0.1-0.6 s before the gain, else one in a throw's path in the last 2.5 s (one gone from view first); with none it still
counts, unplaced (no place, no drops). A placed kill makes an expected pile in the `DropStore`, ends her `Wounds` on
it, and its body is taken for **dying** (no target) for its death animation.

### A fight is a loop of looks
`fight.clear` looks, checks her health (the safety stop may end the hunt from inside any look), works out what to fight
(minus the dying, plus monsters she hit that just went hidden), asks `attack.stance` for one act (throw, jump throw,
jump back, step away, close in, wait), and carries it out with `Actions`: about one throw per attack lock (730 ms plus a
60 ms margin). `fight.kill` shoots a single target; `FightOnTheWay` is the navigator's escort while travelling and its
price of each landing.

### Each throw's key is chosen at the last moment
Just before an attack key goes down, `Actions` asks `Attacks.key` (in every attack mode but 'regular', unless a key
doubt routes it there): which monster the attack will take (the likeliest in its path, not one likely dead), what it
has left (a probability distribution, `attack.choice.Left`), and her MP (the bar less casts the frame can't show yet).
Then `attack.choice.pick`: Lucky Seven, or the regular attack when her MP is under a cast, when nothing is in the way,
or when the regular attack finishes it about as fast. Right before that, `Hunter._still` reads the feed's newest frame
and drops the throw if a kill came in since the look it was decided on.

### Two characters
The thief throws stars (Lucky Seven). The magician casts Magic Claw, which only goes at a body her search picks, and
not again where it showed no effect until new evidence (she or it moves, its bar changes: `Attacks.picks`); her damage
is learned from the monsters' HP bars into a `damage.Book` kept between runs.

### The target-first planner
`Targeting` (on by default since 2026-11-04) is the grind's planner: one primary target and the next, chosen by EXP
over time-to-kill, re-asked at every look and watched frame by frame while her attack lock runs out.

### Safety
Every key goes through the key player, whose watchdog stops everything the moment the game's anti-bot Lie Detector
shows; `Hunter.look` raises `LieDetectorAlarm` then, so a hunt that is only looking stops too. Her HP is checked at
every look and glance against a reserve of her profile's `safety_hits` (3 for the thief) of the map's largest touches:
under it on two looks 0.6 s apart (sooner by her HP number), the safety stop ends the hunt (`HpWatch`, raised at
`health_check` and, with `STOP_ON_LOOK`, at the very look it falls due).

### Why it's built this way
Observers keep every count independent of who drives. Most thresholds come from the live hunts' telemetry (dated in
the comments) or from paired simulator runs, and each switch (`LAST_LOOK`, `STOP_ON_LOOK`, `HIDDEN_WALKS`,
`JITTER_ALL`, ...) keeps the old behaviour one flag away.

No code. The layer rule in its docstring is enforced by `tests/test_architecture.py`, which checks that each gamelab package imports only the layers below it. Behavior sits at the top of the decision stack, over attack, control, motion, localization and perception.

Besides this slice's modules (`hunter`, `fight`, `attacks`, `damage`, `ledger`, `targeting`), the package holds the hunt loop and its modes (`hunt`, `grind`, `patrol`, `tour`, `sweep`, `lootchain`, `looting`, `presence`), her upkeep and stops (`pet`, `safety`, `darts`, `retreat`, `guard`, `vitals`, `bootstrap`), the in-game checks (`keycheck`, `statcheck`, `chatcheck`) and the probes (`probe`), plus `walk`.

modules.tagline: Her senses, keys and books in one object; every look and throw passes through it
modules.summary: The agent object that every hunting command builds once. It owns her Senses, Actions, Looter, Report and the bookkeeping (ledger, drops, wounds, memory, aggro, attack choice), and after every look it counts her EXP gains as kills, measures her HP and touches, reads her facing and checks her health. Its health_check raises the stops (safety, out of darts, key doubts) that end or interrupt a hunt.
modules.details_md:
### What it builds
`Hunter.__init__` makes the whole agent: `Senses` (with the look band `LOOK_UP`..`LOOK_DOWN`, the perception `feed`
and her profile's `Shape`), `Actions` (her keys), a `Looter`, a `Report`, `PetCare`, `DropStore` + `Ledger` + `Wounds`,
`Memory`, `SpawnClock`, `Aggro`, `Attacks`, `DartWatch` (out of darts; the magician gets `MpWatch`, out of MP, instead), `RegularWatch` (her regular attack's key
doubted), a casts watch for Lucky Seven, `MoveWatch`, `HpWatch` (the safety stop), `HerStats` (max HP, level, DEF) and
`Touches` (her measured touches). The attack mode is `attack` (`'choice'`, `'skill'`, `'regular'`); a non-thief
profile (the magician) gets her policy's default mode whatever was asked, and only she gets a `damage.Book`.

### The listeners
Look listeners, in order: `_vitals`, `_heading`, `_others`, `_publish`, `Ledger.on_look`, `DropStore.on_look`,
`Looter.on_look`, `Wounds.on_look`, `Memory.on_look`, `_misses`, `Attacks.on_look`, `_chat_seen`, `_births`, `_aggro`;
then the check `_stop_now`. Throw listeners: `Ledger.on_throw`, `Wounds.on_throw`, `Memory.on_throw`, `Aggro.throw`,
`Attacks.on_throw`, `_tell_feed`, `_key_pick`. The order matters: the ledger reads the gains `_vitals` just counted.

### `_vitals`: EXP, HP and touches after every look
With the feed, a look carries the events since the last one. EXP readings (`feed_reads`) go through the `ExpMeter`;
each `Gain` names the kinds its size fits (`kinds_of`: None, any kind, for a gain no kill explains); `_gained` counts each kill (`exp_events` for `kill()`, `told` for the ledger,
`Report.exp_kills`) and restarts the out-of-darts stretch. HP number reads: a drop with nothing unread between is an
exact touch (`_touched`, written to her touches file, its kind told by its size); a rise of `POTION_RISE_HP` (100) or
more is a potion (her pet drinks them). Touch popups (MISS or damage) go to `_touch_told`; one that took HP sets
`knock_at`, and moves decided within `KNOCK_S` (0.45 s) wait (`fight.knocked_move`). Without a feed, an HP bar drop is a
touch. An HP read of 2% or less right after one of 30% or more isn't believed until the next look (`_doubt_hp`).

### `health_check` and the stops
Asked at every look of a fight, a trip and a hunt-loop pass: potions and pet food (`drink_if_low`), then it raises the
first that's due: `TooStrong`, the safety stop (`HpWatch.due`: HP under her reserve, which `_reserve_check` rebuilds
from the map's kinds, her level, DEF, max HP and measured touches), `OutOfMp` (the magician), `OutOfDarts` (or a
`KeyDoubt` first with `STARS_CHECKED`), key doubts, `ChatDue`, `StatsDue`. With `STOP_ON_LOOK` the safety stop is also
raised at whichever look or glance it falls due on (`_stop_now`, `_glanced`), once a hunt has asked and never while
she retreats.

### `_still`: the last look before a key
With `LAST_LOOK`, once her attack lock has run out, the feed's newest state is read if it is of a frame after her
keys' effect (`Senses.fresh_after`; nothing is waited for, and with no such frame the throw goes): her MP
(`Attacks.glance`), the tracks, MISS popups, and the EXP events not yet drained. A gain naming a kind in the throw's way
(as a copy of her meter reads it), or the target's track marked killed, drops the throw; the caller decides again.

### Facing and the feed
`_heading` reads which way the frame shows her facing (not on a rope) and hands it to `Actions.see`. A strong frame
that disagrees with her keys makes `_retell` tell the feed again, the other way, the throws since her last arrow, hit or
agreeing look (`RETELL_S` 2.5 s back at most), so the tracker binds their kills on the right side.

decisions.what: No potion key: drink_if_low does nothing (her pet drinks her potions).
decisions.why: It logged 'drinking a potion' at every look under potion_hp and drank none (83 times in 3 minutes in the simulator).

decisions.what: Her pet fed by its fullness, read once with no monster within PET_CLEAR and followed in time.
decisions.why: Until then it was fed blind every 10 minutes and only while hunting, and was found at fullness 9.

decisions.what: An HP of 0 right after a high read isn't believed until the next look (_doubt_hp).
decisions.why: On Tree Dungeon her HP read 0% three times in two minutes while the game showed 592/752, each sending her to rest.

decisions.what: No resting: HP staying low raises the safety stop instead of handing control back to rest.
decisions.why: Until 2026-10-26 'HP low' under low_hp stopped the fight and she was sent to rest on the chair (README: No resting).

decisions.what: LAST_LOOK: the feed's newest frame is read once the lock has run out, and a throw dropped if a kill came in.
decisions.why: Live on 2026-10-25 a throw's look was a median 0.57 s old at its key, and 17 throws went out after a gain had shown.

decisions.what: RETELL_S: throws re-told to the feed when a strong frame shows her facing the other way.
decisions.why: On the recording of 2026-10-26 00:20 two of 15 kills were bound to a live monster on the side she hadn't thrown at.

decisions.what: STOP_ON_LOOK: the safety stop raised at the look or glance it is due on.
decisions.why: In the simulator it came up to 1.4 s late at the next health_check, a touch landing in that time in 3 of 42 runs; now 0 s late in 82 runs.

decisions.what: keys_doubted marks a remembered key binding doubted when a doubt can't be checked.
decisions.why: A stale MOVE RIGHT remembered on E, never checked in 12 runs, came back at every start.

decisions.what: feed_reads inserts the EXP value before the first gain when the meter has never read it.
decisions.why: Until then the first reading came with her first kill, and that kill's EXP was lost (R1 of 2026-11-02).

decisions.what: Her walk and climb from her stat window's SPEED by the client's formula.
decisions.why: The user: "Just use panel, no need to measure."

decisions.what: TOP_RATE_ABOVE on, with a touch priced as what follows it.
decisions.why: The user: "keep the rope rule on"; EXP was level within the noise against the hunt's rate.

decisions.what: _key_pick: a 'key_pick' telemetry record of what the game's search would pick at each attack key.
decisions.why: The user's request on the no-hit recordings; nothing she does reads it.

gotchas: health_check raises: every caller of a fight, trip or hunt-loop pass must expect SafetyStop, TooStrong, OutOfDarts, OutOfMp, KeyDoubt, ChatDue and StatsDue; with STOP_ON_LOOK any look or glance can raise the safety stop too (only once a hunt has asked after her health, never while she retreats).
Hunter.look raises client.LieDetectorAlarm whenever the alarm is up.
Listener order matters: the ledger reads the gains _vitals has just counted, and memory reads the ledger's kills.
Report is replaced by a tour at every stop; exp_gains and exp_rises are never reset, so cross-stop counts read those.
A throw can be dropped at its last look (_still): Actions.throw then returns False and nothing is sent; the caller must look again.
The danger property rebuilds attack.danger.of_map(model, her) on every read unless a test set one.
A non-thief profile overrides the asked attack mode with her policy's default, and logs that it did.
The comment on `aggro` says nothing reads it yet, but behavior.targeting's foes_of reads its chasers.

modules.title: Fights
modules.tagline: clear a spot, kill one monster, shoot what's in her way while travelling
modules.summary: The fight loops. clear() fights the monsters in reach look by look (stance, throw, step, wait) until a kill count, a time limit or nothing left in reach, finishing monsters she has hurt before it ends. kill() shoots one target and keeps the shot log. FightOnTheWay is the navigator's escort while she travels and its price for each landing.
modules.details_md:
### `clear`: a fight at a spot
A loop of looks that ends after `seconds` (120), after `max_kills` (10) kills counted as her EXP gains, or when nothing
has been in reach for `patience` (1.5 s; `EMPTY_PATIENCE` 0.4 s when there's nothing to fight at all). Each look:

1. `_place_and_check`: if she isn't placed, wait 0.2 s (give up after `UNPLACED_LOOKS` 10, "lost track of her");
   `h.health_check` (may raise the safety stop); leaving the platform the fight started on ends it ("left platform N").
2. `_targets`: the wanted monsters (of `kinds`; on the `ground` platforms or hers; with `far`, any a star reaches;
   always any within `IN_HER_WAY` 150 on her platform), minus those fading where a kill died (`fade_s`: the kind's
   death animation, else `FADING` 1.2 s) or taken for dying by the ledger, minus the kills her EXP told of
   (`_count_kills`); plus monsters she threw at that went out of sight, kept `HIDDEN_FOR` 1.8 s and thrown at while a
   throw is still worth it (`shots_at` → `Attacks.worth_a_throw`). With `HIDDEN_WALKS` a hidden one heading at her is
   walked on along its track (`hidden_place`).
3. `owed` / `finish_act`: a monster she has hurt (`Hunter.wounds`) in reach or a walk of `FINISH_WALK` 150 along her
   platform is finished before the fight ends.
4. `_take_stance` asks `attack.stance.stance` for one act: `('throw', side)`, `('jump_throw', side[, JumpPlan])`,
   `('jump_back', side[, JumpPlan])`, `('back', side, units[, AWAY])`, `('approach', side, units)` or `('wait',)`
   (a `JumpPlan` carries a jump's timed shot: when its attack key goes, at whom, where she lands). It passes her
   pace (`pace_of`: her lock, monsters' walks from their tracks), her jumps' coverage (`jump_cover`), the map's danger,
   move limits and, for the magician, which monsters she'll cast at. For a throw it keeps everything in the attack's
   path (`_in_path`), since a star hits the first monster in its way, whatever its kind.
5. `knocked_move`: a jump or step decided within `KNOCK_S` of a knock waits 0.05 s for the next look.
6. `_carry_out`: `throw_act` (jittered key, `log_jump`, then `Actions.throw` / `jump_throw` / `jump_back`) or
   `Actions.walk`; with nothing to do, `_idle` sweeps kill spots, loots pending drops, then waits.

When it ends, gains its own looks didn't place are counted (`_count_late`) and the kills on her platform are swept
(`Looter.sweep_after`). `Report.stop` says why it ended.

### Matching a kill to a monster
`_count_kills` takes the monster the ledger bound the gain to by its track (`_tracked_kill`), else `dead_one` over the
last throw's path and her throws of the last `KEYED_KEEP_S` 2.5 s. Its drops go to the end-of-fight sweep if it died on
her platform, else to `Looter.pending` for the tour.

### `kill`: one target
Throws at one monster (`attack.stance.decide`) until her EXP has risen since her first throw (`Hunter.take_exp`):
'killed', 'lost' (unseen `LOST_AFTER` 3 s), 'timeout', 'unreachable' or "lost track of her". It keeps the shot log
`lab/shots2.jsonl`: each throw scored hit, miss or undecided by the target's HP bar (`_score_shots`, `_credit_kill`),
from which a star's reach is measured.

### `FightOnTheWay`: the navigator's escort
Between moves of a hunting trip: a short burst at what's in reach (`shoot`: 3 kills, `GUARD_SECONDS` 15, never walking
after them), a monster in the way of the next move (`clear_way`), one that could touch her on the chain ahead
(`clear_for`, `shot_place`, `shoot_from`), and `landings`, which hands the navigator a `judge(leg, last)` function pricing each leg's landing (in seconds)
against the chain's monster tracks: those seen within `STALE_S` 1.5 s fully; with none of those priced, older tracks and
the platform's unaccounted spawn points at `UNSEEN_PRICE` 0.25 of that.

### Prices
`landing_prices` (`OWN_PRICES`): a touch's HP priced in EXP (its share of her max HP, at the user's potion price
`hunt.HP_PER_MESO` 2 HP a meso and `MESO_EXP` 0.5 EXP a meso), her
EXP a second (`rate_of`: `Hunter.exp_rate`, else `RATE_PRIOR` 6.85, kept within 4x either way), and the share of her
touches that hurt (`HURT_PRIOR` 10 prior touches). `made_rate` blends what she has made with 60 s of the prior: the cost
of a throw's lock.

modules.title: Attacks (each throw's attack)
modules.tagline: Which monster a throw takes, what it has left, and Lucky Seven or the regular attack
modules.summary: Chooses each throw's attack at the moment its key goes out: the monster the attack will take, the HP it has left as a probability distribution, her MP as her bar and her casts say, and then Lucky Seven or the regular attack. It follows every monster she has thrown at (marks) look by look, and runs two failsafes for attacks that hit nothing. For the magician it also refuses casts that would do nothing and learns her damage.
modules.details_md:
Every throw goes through `Actions`, whose attack key asks `Attacks.key(side)` just before the key goes down (in
mode 'regular' only once a key doubt routes it here) (the
fights, the hunt loop, grinding and the navigator's fights alike).

### `key`: the thief's throw
1. **Target**: `aimed` (a jump shot's own target, set by `fight.throw_act`) if it's not dying and worth a throw, else
   `target(side)`: the likeliest monster in the ground attack's path in the last look that searched
   (`ledger.in_path`), never one dying, one a look missed only if `worth_a_throw`; the first less than `DEAD_LIKELY`
   (0.5) dead by her throws, else the likeliest; with nothing in the path, the mark she last threw at that way (within
   `SEEN_MARK_S` 1.8 s, or one no look has that's still worth a throw). No target and nothing a star could take that
   way: no throw at all (`_no_throw`).
2. **What it has left** (`reckon`): an `attack.choice.Left`: the chance of each amount of damage still
   needed to kill it, from the game data's HP,
   less each pending throw's damage distribution with her `miss` share. A look that sees it alive `LANDS_S` (0.6 s)
   after a throw rules out what that throw would have killed it with; so does a frame `KILL_SHOWN_S` (0.4 s) after the
   key with no EXP gain that could be its kill. A believable bar (strictly between 0 and 1) resets it.
3. **Which attack** (`attack.choice.pick`): the regular attack when her MP is under one cast ('MP'), with nothing seen
   in its way, or when it finishes the monster about as fast ('finish'); else Lucky Seven ('damage'). With
   `DEAD_CHOICE` the whole reckoning, dead chance included, decides. Then overrides: the regular attack at a monster no
   look has where a cast's MP isn't worth it ('unseen'); Lucky Seven held or forced by the key checks.
4. A `Mark` on the target records the pending throw; the choice is logged and sent as an 'attack' record.

### Her MP
The bar's share less casts the frame can't show yet. `_believed` keeps her reckoning between the read minus casts
keyed after t − `MP_FIRST_S` (0.21 s) and that minus casts keyed back to t − `MP_SHOWS_S` (0.55 s). A 0 read within
`WARNING_S` (2 s) of a read of `WARNING_STEPS` (9 px of 104) or less is her pet's MP warning, not believed (`_mp_read`).
`glance` reads it again off the newest frame just before the key.

### After every look (`on_look`)
Marks are followed (`seen_again`), landed throws applied, placed kills and dead tracks end their marks, marks unseen
`LOST_S` (3 s) or untouched `FORGET_S` (15 s) are forgotten, throws at monsters no look had are judged
(`_judge_blind`), and the key-doubt watches judge her presses.

### Failsafes
`_landing`: after `UNLANDED_THROWS` (2) throws at one monster with no bar and no EXP since, the next taps the arrow
first. `_watch_hits`: `NO_HIT_ATTACKS` (4) attacks with no monster hit, a second after the 4th: tap the arrow and tell
`Hunter._no_hit` (which keeps a recording).

### The magician (`picks`)
Magic Claw goes only at a body the last look saw that her search picks. `refused` says why not: 'unseen', 'dead',
'no effect' (a `Hold` on the mark), 'no effect from here' (a `Spot` held), 'likely dead'. Her casts at a mark are
judged by the looks that see it again (`_judge`): an effect from `SHOWS_S` on (its bar `PICK_BAR_STEP`/2 lower, a bar
up where none was, any EXP gain, her MISS popup over it) proves the mark; none by `LANDS_S` (up to `JUDGE_BY_S` 3 s)
holds the mark and her spot that way until new evidence (her or it moving `HOLD_MOVED` 20 units, a bar change, a gain,
a cast the other way, or `SPOT_HELD_S` 6 s for a spot). Her damage is learned into a `damage.Book` (`_learn_bar`,
`_learn_kill`).

modules.title: Damage book
modules.tagline: Her attack's damage learned from monsters' HP bars and kept between runs
modules.summary: Learns the magician's Magic Claw damage from what the monsters' HP bars show after her casts: exact damages, misses and 'at least' from kills, fitted by maximum likelihood to a uniform hit range. The fit replaces her profile's prior once 15 exact reads are in, and is kept in her damage file between runs. The thief has no book: her attacks are as measured.
modules.details_md:
The magician's Magic Claw prior (the v83 formula on her stat window: each of a cast's two hits 76-267) was far off:
the bars of 2026-10-29's grinds showed a cast (both hits) doing 254-298 before defence (p10-p90), so a Green Mushroom
(303 damage to kill before its MDD of 30) came out of one cast with about a tenth left nearly every time, where the
prior had 69% of landed casts kill it, reckoned it 50% dead after one, and held her second cast back as 'likely dead'. So her damage is learned from the monsters' HP bars as
she hunts and kept between runs.

### What a read is
`Attacks` adds a `Read` when it can pin one throw's effect:
- **exact**: a bar read between empty and full after exactly one throw whose damage surely showed since the bar before
  (and no throw that may or may not have shown): damage = bar drop × HP × (100 + defence)/100, give or take a bar
  pixel (`BAR_PX` 46 px of fill, at least `TOL_MIN` 3);
- **miss**: a drop under `MISS_PX` (0.5 px) after a bar was read before;
- **at least**: a kill placed after exactly one such throw: it did at least what the monster had left.
Nothing is learned with another player near the monster (a bar shows anyone's damage).

### The fit
A hit's damage is a whole number from lo to hi, uniformly; `hits` per throw. `_cdf` treats one hit as uniform, two as
a triangle, more as a normal. `fit` maximises the likelihood over a 48 × 64 grid of (lo, hi), then a finer 21 × 21 grid
around the best. Each exact read is an outlier with chance `OUTLIER` (0.05), each kill with `OUTLIER_KILL` (0.15); a
kill's 'at least' more than `KILL_SLACK` (15%) over the largest exact read is dropped. The fit is used from `MIN_EXACT`
(15) exact reads; the miss share from `MIN_MISSES` (20) judged throws. Only reads of her level and `LEVELS_BACK` (1)
under it count.

### The Book
`Book` keeps `{attack key: {hits, reads, fit}}` in her damage file, the newest `KEEP` (400) reads each. `add` refits at
most every `REFIT_S` (10 s) on a daemon thread and bumps `version` when the fit changes; `Attacks.on_look` sees the new
version and takes `Book.attack(prior)` (the prior with lo/hi replaced) and `Book.miss`. It saves every `SAVE_S` (60 s)
and at exit, writing a temp file then replacing, so the file is never half written.

modules.title: Ledger: kills, wounds and drops
modules.tagline: Every EXP gain placed on a monster; her wounds; every pile she knows of
modules.summary: The hunt's bookkeeping, kept up from every look and throw. The Ledger turns each EXP gain into a Kill placed on the monster her attack took (the tracker's binding first, else her throws' paths) and keeps which tracks are dead. Wounds lists monsters she hurt and hasn't killed. The DropStore keeps every pile, its worth and how likely it still lies there.
modules.details_md:
Step 4 of `gamelab/docs/hunt-modes.md`. Three observers kept up from every look (`on_look`) and every throw (`on_throw`), whoever takes them. The hunt loop
reads the drop store; the fights and the hunt loop read the wounds; almost everything reads which monsters are dead.

### The ledger (`Ledger`)
Each new EXP gain (`Hunter.exp_gains`, with when it showed and the kind it named: `gains_told`) becomes a `Kill`.
`_place` puts it on a monster:
1. the track the perception service's tracker bound the gain to (`_bound`: a track whose gain time is within
   `TRACK_GAIN_S` 0.02 s), its throw (one keyed 0.1-0.6 s before, `GAIN_AFTER_KEY`) used up: one star, one kill;
2. else a monster of the named kind in the path of a throw keyed 0.1-0.6 s before the gain;
3. else one in a path of the last `STAR_WINDOW` (2.5 s) of throws (or that long before the previous look),
   preferring monsters now gone from view, and with `PLAYER_KILLS` one by another player last;
4. else unplaced: counted for its kind, no place, no drops (`KIND_ANY` False: no other kind is tried).

A placed kill asks the drop store for an expected pile. For `FOLLOW_S` (3 s) a tracked kill follows its track as it
walks on, and moves when the tracker re-binds the gain. `_dead_of` keeps `dead` (track ids dead or dying, kept
`DEAD_KEEP_S` 15 s), `theirs` (other players' kills) and `unsure` (bound but no death seen yet).

### Who is dying (`dying`)
A monster is no target while its track is in `dead`, or a kill of hers is bound to it (for its death animation plus
`BOUND_LASTS_S` 1 s while seen); without tracks, while its kind's death animation (`DIE_S` 0.66 s default) runs from the
placing look, if it's the nearest of its kind within `DYING_DX` (40) of where the kill was placed.

### What a throw can take (`in_path`)
The monsters an attack from the ground that way can take, likeliest first (`reach.take_chances` by bodies), without
those whose star terrain stops (unless the claw reaches them). Used by the ledger, wounds and `Attacks.target`.

### Her wounds (`Wounds`)
A monster in a recent throw's path whose HP bar shows up or changes by more than `WOUND_HURT` (0.02) is hers. It's
followed until a kill is placed on it, its track dies, it's unseen `WOUND_LOST_S` (3 s), or `WOUND_S` (15 s) pass since
it was first hurt. `fight.owed` finishes these.

### The drop store (`DropStore`)
Every pile she knows of (`Pile`): expected at a placed kill (worth its kind's expected drops), confirmed or emptied by
each look's loot and each strip of drops perception searched since the last look. Each drop seen goes to its nearest
pile within `LOOT_REACH` (60); unclaimed drops make another's pile. A pile is gone after two empty sightings
`EMPTY_LOOKS` (1.5 s) apart, at least `SETTLE` (3 s) after its kill; one of hers seen gone that a sighting within
`REVIVE_S` (30 s) shows again was only missed. How likely it still lies there is `survival` by its age: hers alone for
`OWN_S` (15 s), then taken at `TAKE_RATE` 0.05 a minute, gone at the expiry pass after `EXPIRE_S` (180 s) +
`EXPIRE_PASS_S` (60 s); others' by the live curve.

modules.title: Targeting (the target-first planner)
modules.tagline: The grind's planner: one primary target, the next, and the plan against it
modules.summary: The grind's target-first planner, on by default since 2026-11-04. At each look it builds the character's state and the candidate monsters (with the whole screen, every monster on it), lets attack.target's Chooser pick the primary and the next by EXP over time, and plans against the primary: the stance's act, a walk to a place that works, or a trip. While her attack lock runs out it watches every frame for a monster coming at her or a better newborn, and it decides when drops go first.
modules.details_md:
The grind's fight on a platform, as the user asked on 2026-11-04: decide which one monster to hit and plan against
that. `Targeting` turns each look into `attack.target`'s `Her` and `Foe`s and keeps a `Chooser` (the primary target and
the next). Only `behavior.grind` builds one (when `on()`), and it hooks `watch_lock` into `Actions.lock_watch`.
Everything else about a stop (where she goes next, potions, the safety stop, the Lie Detector) stays the grind's.

### The choice (`decide`)
At each pass: `pace_of` (her lock and monsters' walks), `her_at` (her platform, place, facing, danger, stand limits,
jump hits, and with the whole screen the navigator's route times), `foes_of` (the hunt's targets, the look's monsters of the
kinds she hunts plus any kind on or beside her platform, and with `screen_on` the rest of the screen and those the look
missed; a target set aside is left out). Each `Foe` has its kind's EXP,
its kill time (`Attacks.kill_s`), the chance it's there and alive (`Attacks.chance`, times 1 − her reckoned dead chance;
the magician's held ones × `HELD_P` 0.25), its walk (track, or her aggro belief's chase) and a newborn's fade. The
`Chooser` ranks by EXP over time to an attack plus kill time and keeps the primary unless another beats it by its
margin (1.3). On a trip, monsters too close come first.

### The plan (`plan`, `walk_step`, `trip_act`)
The stance's own act at the primary; with nothing from where she stands, the walk to the nearest place that works
(`attack.target.places`, the first whose way the navigator finds clear, at most `WALK_STEP` 100 units at once); off her
platform, a trip there. A target with nothing to do against it is set aside for `NO_WAY_S` (0.5 s) so she never idles on one.

### While her lock runs out (`watch_lock`)
No key can go, and a look would be the wrong one to decide on, so each frame (`FRAME_S`, 1/15 s) the feed's newest
state is read: a monster coming at her that isn't her target, or a newborn that beats the primary by the margin, calls
the attack off (`False`) and the next pass decides at once.

### Drops
`loot_allow`: a pile near its end (`LOOT_DUE_S` 30 s of its 180 s left), any pile when nothing is on the screen
(`quiet`), or one on her platform already seen or still landing may cost anything (`LOOT_ALL`); others `LOOT_FRESH`
(3 s) on her way (none while the sweep asks for her platform alone). `pile_first`: a pile goes before the primary only when it would
expire first, or it's nearer than a primary she must walk to; never against a monster coming at her.

### Switches
`GAMELAB_TARGET` (on), `GAMELAB_SCREEN` (on), `GAMELAB_LOOT_CHAIN` (via `lootchain.on`), `GAMELAB_STAY_OR_GO` ('0' by
default: a trip's landings asked, her round weighed against what the screen had lately, `_worth`).

flows.title: What happens after every look
flows.summary: Whoever takes a look (a fight, the navigator, the looter, the hunt loop), the same listeners run in the same order, so EXP, HP, kills, drops, wounds and the attack reckoning are always current.

steps.text: Checks the Lie Detector alarm (raises if up), then asks Senses for a look, drops limited to mesos if her item tabs are full.
Takes the feed's state (or the eyes' frame), places it on the map as a Scene, then calls every listener and every check.
HP doubted or read exactly (touches measured), level, unseen kinds, the safety watch fed; EXP readings through the meter, each gain counted as kills (_gained); touches told.
Her facing off the frame to Actions.see; a strong disagreement re-tells recent throws to the feed.
New gains become Kills placed on monsters (the tracker's binding first); dead tracks updated; tracked kills followed.
Drop strips and the look's loot confirm, empty or revive piles; unclaimed drops make others' piles.
Kills close wounds; monsters in recent throws' paths with a bar new or changed become wounds.
MP believed, marks followed and reckoned, placed kills end marks, the no-hit watch runs.
The check after the listeners: `gamelab stop` asked, or the safety stop due, raises here (STOP_ON_LOOK).

flows.title: From a fight's look to a thrown key
flows.summary: One pass of clear(): the look, what to fight, the stance, and the throw, whose attack key is chosen and checked at the last moment before Actions sends it to the key player.
flows.trigger: fight.clear's loop (the hunt loop, a tour stop, or FightOnTheWay)

steps.text: Looks (Hunter.look) unless the kill count, time or patience is up.
Placed? Then Hunter.health_check, which may raise the safety stop; a new platform ends the fight.
Wanted minus fading/dying/killed, kills counted, plus hidden ones still worth a throw.
attack.stance chooses throw / jump throw / jump back / step / approach / wait; a throw's path is kept for kill matching.
A jump or step decided while a knock may still move her waits for the next look.
_carry_out calls it for a throwing act: jitters a jump's attack key, logs it, and calls Actions.throw / jump_throw / jump_back (False back if the throw is dropped at its last look).
Waits out her attack lock (Targeting.watch_lock frame by frame in a grind), then asks `still`.
Reads the feed's newest frame: a kill come in, or the target dead by its track, drops the throw (False).
Picks the target, reckons what it has left, chooses Lucky Seven or the regular attack (or no throw), records a Mark.
Tells the throw listeners the key's time: Ledger.on_throw, Wounds.on_throw, Attacks.on_throw, Hunter._tell_feed; then the plan goes to the key player.
Back from throw_act: a throw that went is noted in FightState (its path kept for kill matching) and counted in the Report; a dropped one is decided again at the next look.

flows.title: From an EXP gain to a placed kill and an expected pile
flows.summary: How her EXP number rising becomes a kill of a particular monster, a pile to pick up, and a body no throw goes at while it dies.
flows.trigger: The perception service's step reads her EXP number changing (an 'exp_gain' event)

steps.text: The look's EXP events as readings for her meter (with the value before the first gain if never read).
ExpMeter.update turns readings into Gains naming the kinds their sizes fit.
Each kill named goes to exp_events (kill()), told (the ledger) and Report.exp_kills; out of darts restarts.
The gains with their kinds: throws keyed KILL_SHOWN_S before with no matching gain didn't kill.
The gain placed: the tracker's bound track, else the throw 0.1-0.6 s before, else recent paths, else unplaced.
A placed kill expects a pile where it died, worth its kind's expected drops.
The fight takes the tracked monster (or dead_one in its paths) as dead, counts it, and keeps its drop spot.
From then on, that monster's body is no target (dead track, or nearest a fresh kill of its kind) until it fades.

flows.title: The magician's damage learned from the bars
flows.summary: How her Magic Claw's damage range is learned from HP bars and fed back into her reckoning, across runs.
flows.trigger: A look that reads a bar on a monster she cast at (or a kill placed on it)

steps.text: Only for a non-thief profile with Magic Claw bound: a damage.Book on her damage file.
Exactly one cast surely shown since the bar before: its damage (bar drop x HP x defence factor) or a miss.
A kill after exactly one such cast: it did at least what the monster had left.
Keeps the read, refits on a 'damage-fit' thread at most every REFIT_S, saves every SAVE_S.
Maximum likelihood (lo, hi) on a coarse then fine grid, from 15 exact reads on.
On the next look after the version changes: her skill's lo/hi and miss share from the book.
